chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Muyassir, who said:
Al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام said:

Indeed, among what the revelation brought down from the heaven is this: if the son of Adam had two valleys flowing with gold and silver, he would seek a third beside them. O son of Adam, your belly is only a sea among seas and a valley among valleys; nothing fills it except dust.

key_terms.الْوَحْيُ: divine revelation sent down from heaven
key_terms.بَطْنُكَ: your belly, referring to appetite and desire
key_terms.ذَهَبًا وَ فِضَّةً: gold and silver, symbolizing worldly wealth
key_terms.لِابْنِ آدَمَ: the human being, as a descendant of Adam
key_terms.وَادِيَيْنِ: two valleys, used here as an image of abundant possession

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach about greed for wealth and the insatiable nature of human desire?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that human greed and desire for worldly accumulation are naturally unending unless restrained. It warns that material wealth does not satisfy the human appetite, and that only death, symbolized by dust, finally brings worldly craving to an end.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5912 - Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Maysar that
Abu Abdullah Imam Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (as) said:

"Indeed, among what was revealed in the divine revelation from the heavens is that if the son of Adam had two flowing valleys of gold and silver, he would still seek a third. O' son of Adam! Your stomach is but an ocean among oceans and a valley among valleys; nothing will fill it except dust."
